A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a workflow system can be seen as a view on the underlying data model.
the expressiveness of a workflow formalism depends on the underlying data model, the view, and the control mechanism used.
a workflow specification language should be chosen based on the expressiveness needed and the underlying data model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comparison of workflow specification formalism is not only a question of the expressiveness of the underlying data model.
the choice of a workflow specification mechanism is largely determined by the views of interest.

the choice of a workflow specification language should not be based on a simple comparison of its expressiveness with respect to a fixed set of workflow control mechanisms, but rather with respect to the expressiveness of the workflow views that are relevant for the application domain.
